units.zh: 國之有食貨，猶人之有飲食也。
units.en: For a state, grain and goods are what food and drink are for a person.
units.literal: A state has food and goods as a person has drink and food.

units.zh: 人非飲食不生，國非食貨不立。
units.en: A person cannot survive without nourishment, nor can a state endure without its economic foundation.
units.literal: Without drink and food a person cannot live; without food and goods a state cannot stand.

units.zh: 然燧人、庖犧能為飲食之道以教人，而不能使人無飲食之疾。
units.en: Even Suiren and Fuxi could teach mankind how to prepare food and drink, yet they could not spare people every ill that diet brings.
units.literal: Yet Suiren and Paoxi were able to teach people the ways of drink and food, yet could not make people free of ailments from drink and food.

units.zh: 三王能為食貨之政以遺後世，而不能使後世無食貨之弊。
units.en: The Three Kings could hand down sound policies on public finance, yet they could not keep later ages from the abuses those policies invite.
units.literal: The Three Kings were able to bequeath to later ages policies on food and goods, yet could not make later ages free of abuses in food and goods.

units.zh: 唯善養生者如不欲食啖，而飲食自不闕焉，故能適饑飽之宜，可以疾少而長壽。
units.en: Only those who truly know how to care for the body eat as though indifferent to appetite, yet never go short of nourishment; they regulate hunger and fullness so well that they suffer few illnesses and live long.
units.literal: Only one skilled in nurturing life is like one who does not desire to eat and chew, yet drink and food of themselves are not lacking, so he can suit the appropriate measure of hunger and satiety and thereby have few ailments and long life.

units.zh: 善裕國者初不事貨殖，而食貨自不乏焉，故能制豐約之節，可以弊少而長治。
units.en: A ruler who truly enriches his realm does not obsess over commercial profit, yet grain and goods remain abundant; he can modulate plenty and restraint so that abuses are few and governance endures.
units.literal: One skilled in enriching a state at first does not engage in profit-seeking, yet food and goods of themselves are not scarce, so he can regulate abundance and restraint and thereby have few abuses and long good order.

units.zh: 金於食貨，其立法也周，其取民也審。
units.en: In matters of food and goods, the Jin fashioned laws with care and drew revenue from the people with exacting precision.
units.literal: For the Jin in food and goods, their lawmaking was comprehensive and their extraction from the people careful.

units.zh: 太祖肇造，減遼租稅，規模遠矣。
units.en: At the dynasty's founding, Taizu cut Liao-era rents and taxes, setting a far-sighted example from the start.
units.literal: When Taizu first founded the dynasty, he reduced Liao rents and taxes—the vision was far-reaching indeed.

units.zh: 熙宗、海陵之世，風氣日開，兼務遠略，君臣講求財用之制，切切然以是為先務。
units.en: Under Xizong and Hailing the realm grew cosmopolitan; court and emperor together obsessed over fiscal institutions, making finance their foremost concern.
units.literal: In the reigns of Xizong and Hailing, customs daily opened up; they pursued distant designs together, ruler and ministers alike discussing systems of fiscal use, urgently taking this as their foremost task.

units.zh: 雖以世宗之賢，儲積之志曷嘗一日而忘之。
units.en: Even the worthy Emperor Shizong never let a single day pass without thought for building up reserves.
units.literal: Even given Shizong's worthiness, the will to accumulate reserves—when did he forget it even for a day?

units.zh: 章宗彌文煟興，邊費亦廣，食貨之議不容不急。
units.en: Zhangzong's reign saw cultural brilliance—and soaring frontier costs; debate over finance could hardly wait.
units.literal: Under Zhangzong culture blazed and flourished, frontier expenses too grew wide; discussion of food and goods could not but be urgent.

units.zh: 宣宗南遷，國土日蹙，汙池數罟，往往而然。
units.en: After Xuanzong withdrew south, territory shrank daily; exhausted pools fished with net upon net became the norm.
units.literal: When Xuanzong moved south, the realm daily contracted; stagnant pools with nets laid one upon another—this came to pass everywhere.

units.zh: 考其立國以來，所謂食貨之法，犖犖大者曰租稅、銅錢、交鈔三者而已。
units.en: Looking back from the dynasty's founding, the main pillars of economic policy were only three: land rent and tax, copper coinage, and paper notes.
units.literal: Examining from the founding of the state, the so-called laws of food and goods, the outstanding great ones are only three: rent-tax, copper cash, and paper notes.

units.zh: 三者之法數變而數窮。
units.en: Each of these three policies changed again and again until every expedient was spent.
units.literal: The laws of the three repeatedly changed until methods were exhausted.

units.zh: 官田曰租，私田曰稅。
units.en: Rent applied to state lands, tax to private holdings.
units.literal: Official fields are called zu, private fields are called shui.

units.zh: 租稅之外算其田園屋舍車馬牛羊樹藝之數，及其藏鏹多寡，征錢曰物力。
units.en: Beyond rent and tax the state assessed gardens, dwellings, horses, livestock, orchards, and hidden hoards of silver, collecting a cash levy called the property assessment.
units.literal: Beyond rent and tax they calculated gardens, houses, carriages, horses, cattle, sheep, planted trees, and the amount of hidden silver, levying money called wuli.

units.zh: 物力之征，上自公卿大夫，下逮民庶，無苟免者。
units.en: The property levy reached from highest ministers down to humble subjects—no one escaped on petty pretext.
units.literal: In the collection of wuli, from dukes, ministers, and grandees down to the common populace, none received casual exemption.

units.zh: 近臣出使外國，歸必增物力錢，以其受饋遺也。
units.en: Court favorites returning from foreign missions invariably had their property assessments raised, on the ground that they had accepted gifts abroad.
units.literal: Close ministers sent on missions abroad, on returning were always required to increase their wuli assessment, because they had received gifts.

units.zh: 猛安謀克戶又有所謂牛頭稅者，宰臣有納此稅，庭陛間諮及其增減，則州縣徵求于小民蓋可知矣。
units.en: Jurchen meng'an-mouke households also paid the so-called ox-head tax; when grand councilors themselves paid it and the emperor asked at court whether levies had risen or fallen, one may infer how county officials wrung the common people.
units.literal: Meng'an mouke households further had what was called the ox-head tax; when chief ministers paid this tax, the throne inquired about its increase or decrease in the audience hall—then how the prefectures and counties squeezed the small folk may be known.

units.zh: 故物力之外又有鋪馬、軍須、輸庸、司吏、河夫、桑皮故紙等錢，名目瑣細，不可殫述。
units.en: Beyond the property tax came relay horses, military provisions, corvée, clerks' fees, river workers, mulberry bark, wastepaper charges, and countless other dues too numerous to list.
units.literal: Thus beyond wuli there were further the horse relay, military supplies, corvée transport, clerk, river laborer, mulberry bark and scrap paper and other levies, categories minute and inexhaustible to recount.

units.zh: 其為戶有數等，有課役戶、不課役戶、本戶、雜戶、正戶、監戶、官戶、奴婢戶、二稅戶。
units.en: Households fell into many grades: liable for corvée, exempt, original, miscellaneous, regular, supervised, official, bond, and double-tax categories.
units.literal: As to households there were several grades: duty-paying household, non-duty household, original household, miscellaneous household, regular household, supervised household, official household, slave household, double-tax household.

units.zh: 有司始以三年一籍，後變為通檢，又為推排。
units.en: Officials first took a household census every three years, then shifted to nationwide inspection, then to reassessment and re-ranking.
units.literal: The authorities at first registered households once every three years, later changed to comprehensive inspection, then again to reorganization by assessment.

units.zh: 凡戶隸州縣者，與隸猛安謀克，其輸納高下又各不同。
units.en: Those registered under civil prefectures paid on different terms than those under meng'an-mouke units, and rates differed again between them.
units.literal: All households subordinate to prefectures and counties, as against those subordinate to meng'an mouke—their payments high and low again each differed.

units.zh: 法之初行，唯恐不密，言事者謂其厲民，即命罷之。
units.en: When the policy first took force, officials dreaded any laxity; critics called it oppressive and the court at once ordered it stopped.
units.literal: When the law first went into effect, they feared lest it not be strict; memorialists said it harried the people and they were immediately ordered to abolish it.

units.zh: 罷之未久，會計者告用乏，又即舉行。
units.en: Hardly had it been abolished when treasurers warned of shortages and it was hurriedly restored.
units.literal: Not long after abolishing it, accountants reported supplies exhausted and it was immediately revived.

units.zh: 其罷也志以便民，而民未見德。
units.en: Abolition aimed to ease the burden, yet the people felt no relief.
units.literal: In abolishing it the intent was to benefit the people, yet the people did not perceive grace.

units.zh: 其行也志以足用，而用不加饒。
units.en: Enforcement aimed to fill the treasury, yet revenue scarcely increased.
units.literal: In enforcing it the intent was to fill needs, yet supplies did not grow more ample.

units.zh: 一時君臣節用之言不絕告誡。
units.en: For a time the throne and ministers never ceased preaching thrift.
units.literal: For a time admonitions on frugality from ruler and ministers never ceased.

units.zh: 嘗自計其國用，數亦浩瀚，若足支歷年者，郡縣稍遇歲侵，又遽不足，竟莫詰其故焉。
units.en: They once tallied state expenditure—figures vast enough to seem adequate for years—yet a county touched by modest harvest failure would find funds suddenly wanting, and no one ever traced why.
units.literal: They once calculated their state expenditures—the figures too were vast, as if enough to last years—yet when a prefecture or county met slight crop failure they were suddenly insufficient, and in the end no one examined the reason.

units.zh: 至於銅錢、交鈔之弊，蓋有甚者。
units.en: The disorders in copper coin and paper currency were worse still.
units.literal: As for the abuses in copper cash and paper notes, there were indeed graver ones.

units.zh: 初用遼、宋舊錢，雖劉豫所鑄，豫廢，亦兼用之。
units.en: At first old Liao and Song coins circulated; even coins of Liu Yu's puppet regime remained in use after his state fell.
units.literal: At first they used old Liao and Song coins; even what Liu Yu cast, when Yu was abolished they still used together.

units.zh: 正隆而降，始議鼓鑄，民間銅禁甚至，銅不給用，漸興窯冶。
units.en: From the Zhenglong era they debated minting; copper bans on the populace grew fierce, supply failed, and private smelters multiplied.
units.literal: From Zhenglong downward they began to discuss minting; the ban on civilian copper was very severe, copper not enough for use, and smelting works gradually arose.

units.zh: 凡產銅地脈，遺吏境內訪察無遣，且及外界，而民用銅器不可闕者，皆造於官而鬻之。
units.en: Every copper deposit was combed by officials inside and even outside the realm; everyday bronze ware the people required had to be forged in government shops and sold back to them.
units.literal: Wherever copper veins occurred, they sent officials to search within the borders without omission, reaching even beyond the borders; and what the people could not do without—copper vessels—all were made at government workshops and sold.

units.zh: 既而官不勝煩，民不勝病，乃聽民冶銅造器，而官為立價以售，此銅法之變也。
units.en: When bureaucracy and populace alike were overwhelmed, the state allowed private copperware while fixing official sale prices—thus the copper policy shifted.
units.literal: Then the government could not bear the trouble, the people could not bear the burden; they then permitted the people to smelt copper and make vessels while the government set prices for sale—this was the change in copper law.

units.zh: 若錢法之變，則鼓鑄未廣，斂散無方，已見壅滯。
units.en: Coin policy changed too: minting never spread widely, collection and release lacked method, and currency already clogged.
units.literal: As for changes in coin law, minting was not wide, gathering and dispersing had no method, and stagnation was already seen.

units.zh: 初恐官庫多積，錢不及民，立法廣布。
units.en: First they feared treasury hoards would keep coin from the people and legislated wide circulation.
units.literal: At first they feared government treasuries would accumulate much and coin would not reach the people, so they legislated wide distribution.

units.zh: 繼恐民多匿錢，乃設存留之限，開告訐之路，犯者繩以重罰，卒莫能禁。
units.en: Next they feared hoarding, imposed retention caps, encouraged informers, and punished offenders severely—yet still could not stop private storage.
units.literal: Then they feared the people would hoard much coin and set retention limits, opened channels for informing, bound violators with heavy penalties, yet in the end could not stop it.

units.zh: 州縣錢艱，民間自鑄，私錢苦惡特甚。
units.en: Counties faced coin famine; people minted illicit cash of wretched quality.
units.literal: Prefectures and counties found coin scarce; the people themselves cast privately, and illicit coin was wretchedly bad indeed.

units.zh: 乃以官錢五百易其一千，其策愈下。
units.en: The state then traded five hundred official coins for one thousand private ones—a policy that sank lower still.
units.literal: They then exchanged official coin five hundred for illicit one thousand—the policy grew worse still.

units.zh: 及改鑄大錢，所准加重，百計流通，卒莫獲效。
units.en: They reissued heavy coins at higher nominal value and tried every scheme to force circulation, all in vain.
units.literal: When they changed to casting large coin, the standard value increased; they contrived every scheme for circulation yet in the end obtained no effect.

units.zh: 濟以鐵錢，鐵不可用，權以交鈔，錢重鈔輕，相去懸絕，物價騰踴，鈔至不行。
units.en: Iron coin followed, proved unusable, and paper notes took their place—yet heavy metal and light notes diverged wildly, prices surged, and notes died in the market.
units.literal: They supplemented with iron coin; iron could not be used, so they relied on paper notes; coin heavy and notes light, the gap vast, prices soared, and notes ceased to circulate.

units.zh: 權以銀貨，銀弊又滋，救亦無策，遂罷銅錢，專用交鈔、銀貨。
units.en: Silver filled the gap, bred new abuse, and remedies failed—copper was abandoned for notes and silver alone.
units.literal: They relied on silver goods; silver abuses again grew; relief had no policy, and they abolished copper cash, using only paper notes and silver goods exclusively.

units.zh: 然而二者之弊乃甚于錢，在官利於用大鈔，而大鈔出多，民益見輕。
units.en: Yet both vexed worse than coin: officials favored large notes, flooded them into circulation, and the people valued them ever less.
units.literal: Yet the abuses of the two were worse than coin: in office they profited from using large notes, and many large notes issued so the people saw them as lighter still.

units.zh: 在私利於得小鈔，而小鈔入多，國亦無補。
units.en: Commoners preferred small notes; masses of small notes flowed in yet the treasury gained nothing.
units.literal: Among the people they profited from obtaining small notes, and many small notes entered so the state too had no benefit.

units.zh: 於是，禁官不得用大鈔，已而恐民用銀而不用鈔，則又責民以鈔納官，以示必用。
units.en: Officials were barred from large notes; fearing silver would displace notes, they then compelled payment in notes to prove notes were mandatory.
units.literal: Thereupon they forbade officials from using large notes; then fearing the people would use silver and not notes, they again required the people to pay notes to government offices to show they must be used.

units.zh: 先造二十貫至百貫例，後造二百貫至千貫例，先後輕重不倫，民益眩惑。
units.en: Denominations ran from twenty to a hundred strings, later two hundred to a thousand—successive issues mismatched weight and value until the public was thoroughly bewildered.
units.literal: First they made denominations from twenty strings to one hundred strings in example, later two hundred strings to one thousand strings in example—first and later light and heavy not in order, the people grew more dazzled and confused.

units.zh: 及不得已，則限以年數，限以地方，公私受納限以分數，由是民疑日深。
units.en: Desperate measures followed—time limits, regional limits, fractional acceptance for public and private use—deepening public distrust daily.
units.literal: When there was no help for it, they limited by years, limited by region, public and private acceptance limited by fractions; thereby popular suspicion daily deepened.

units.zh: 其間，易交鈔為寶券，寶券未久更作通寶，准銀並用。
units.en: Notes became treasure certificates, then universal treasure notes redeemable alongside silver.
units.literal: In between, they changed paper notes to treasure certificates; treasure certificates not long they made again into universal treasure, equated with silver for joint use.

units.zh: 通寶未久複作寶泉，寶泉未久織綾印鈔，名曰珍貨。
units.en: Universal treasure became treasure spring currency, then silk-woven printed notes called precious goods.
units.literal: Universal treasure not long they made again treasure spring; treasure spring not long they wove silk and printed notes, named precious goods.

units.zh: 珍貨未久複作寶會，汔無定制，而金祚訖矣。
units.en: Precious goods yielded to treasure tally—until regulations vanished altogether and the Jin dynasty expired.
units.literal: Precious goods not long they made again treasure tally; in the end no fixed regulation, and the Jin mandate ended.

units.zh: 曆觀自古財聚民散，以至亡國，若鹿台、钜橋之類，不足論也。
units.en: History shows states ruined by amassing wealth while dispersing the people—think of King Zhou's Lutai or the Juqiao hoard—cases too familiar to rehearse.
units.literal: Looking through antiquity, gathering wealth while scattering the people until the state perished—like Lutai and Juqiao types—need not be discussed.

units.zh: 其國亡財匱，比比有之，而國用之屈，未有若金季之甚者。
units.en: Fallen realms often went bankrupt together, yet no fiscal collapse matched the Jin in its twilight.
units.literal: Perished states with exhausted wealth were common enough, yet the bending of state use had none so severe as in the Jin's final years.

units.zh: 金之為政，常有恤民之志，而不能已苛征之令，徒有聚斂之名，而不能致富國之實。
units.en: Jin rulers often meant to spare the people yet could not halt heavy exactions; they bore the name of revenue but never achieved true national wealth.
units.literal: The Jin in government constantly had a will to pity the people, yet could not stop harsh levies; they only had the name of gathering and amassing, yet could not attain the substance of enriching the state.

units.zh: 及其亡也，括粟、闌糴，一切掊克之政靡不為之。
units.en: In the end they imposed grain requisitions, monopoly purchases, and every conceivable form of squeeze.
units.literal: When they perished, conscripting grain, blocking grain sales—for every policy of crushing extortion they did nothing that was not done.

units.zh: 加賦數倍，豫借數年，或欲得鈔則豫賣下年差科。
units.en: Levies multiplied severalfold, taxes were collected years ahead, and notes were procured by selling next year's corvée quotas in advance.
units.literal: They multiplied levies several fold, advanced levies several years in advance, or if they wished to obtain notes they sold next year's corvée assignments in advance.

units.zh: 高琪為相，議至榷油。
units.en: Under Gao Qi as chief councilor, debate extended even to a state oil monopoly.
units.literal: When Gao Qi was prime minister, discussion reached even to monopolizing oil.

units.zh: 進納濫官，輒售空名宣敕，或欲與以五品正班。
units.en: Buyers of office peddled hollow imperial commissions or bargained for proper fifth-rank regular posts.
units.literal: Those advancing tribute for corrupt offices routinely sold empty titles of imperial commissions, or sought to grant them fifth-rank regular court rank.

units.zh: 僧道入粟，始自度牒，終至德號、綱副威儀、寺觀主席亦量其貲而鬻之。
units.en: Selling offices to clergy began with ordination slips and ended with honorary religious titles, deputy ordination rights, ritual insignia, and abbot's seats—priced to the bidder's purse.
units.literal: Monks and Daoists paying grain began with ordination certificates and ended with virtuous titles, assistant preceptors, ritual regalia, and abbacy chairs—all sold according to their wealth.

units.zh: 甚而丁憂鬻以求仕，監戶鬻以從良，進士出身鬻至及第。
units.en: Worse still, men sold mourning obligations for posts, supervised households bought commoner status, and examination credentials were sold through to full passing.
units.literal: More extreme: during mourning they sold for appointment; supervised households sold for release to commoner status; jinshi graduates sold even to passing the examinations.

units.zh: 又甚而叛臣劇盜之效順，無金帛以備賞激，動以王爵固結其心，重爵不蔇，則以國姓賜之。
units.en: Rebels and bandits who submitted, unappeased by gold or silk, were bound with princely titles; when titles ran short, the imperial surname itself was granted.
units.literal: More extreme still: when rebel chieftains and notorious bandits submitted, with no gold or silk to reward and stimulate them, they routinely used princely ranks to bind their hearts; when noble ranks were not enough they bestowed the imperial clan surname.

units.zh: 名實混淆，倫法颻壞，皆不暇顧，國欲不亂，其可得乎？
units.en: Titles and reality mingled, laws collapsed unattended—how could order endure?
units.literal: Names and substance confused, norms and law scattered in ruin—all unattended; if the state did not fall into disorder, how could it be obtained?

units.zh: 迨夫宋絕歲幣而不許和，貪其淮南之蓄，謀以力取，至使樞府武騎盡于南伐。
units.en: When Song ended yearly tribute and refused peace, Jin coveted Huainan's granaries and resolved on conquest until the Privy Council's cavalry was spent in the south.
units.literal: When at last Song ended the annual tribute and would not permit peace, coveting their stores in Huainan, they plotted to take by force, until the Privy Council's martial riders were exhausted in the southern campaign.

units.zh: 訛可、時全之出，初志得糧，後乃尺寸無補，三軍僨亡，我師壓境，兵財俱困，無以禦之。
units.en: Campaigns under Eke and Shi Quan aimed first at grain and ultimately gained nothing; armies were ruined, foes pressed the frontier, and troops and treasury alike were spent defenseless.
units.literal: The campaigns of Eke and Shi Quan's departure—at first they hoped to gain grain, later not even an inch's benefit; the three armies perished in ruin, our army pressed the border, troops and wealth both trapped, with nothing to resist.

units.zh: 故志金之食貨者，不能不為之掩卷而興慨也。
units.en: Whoever chronicles Jin finance must close the scroll and sigh.
units.literal: Therefore one recording the Jin's food and goods cannot but close the scroll and sigh.

units.zh: 《傳》曰：「作法於涼，其弊猶貪。
units.en: The Zuo Commentary says: "Make law from leniency, and its abuse will still be greed.
units.literal: The Commentary says: "Making law from leniency, its abuse is still greed.

units.zh: 作法於貪，弊將若何。」
units.en: Make law from greed—what then will its abuse become?"
units.literal: Making law from greed—what will the abuse be like?"

units.zh: 金起東海，其俗純實，可與返古。
units.en: The Jin arose on the Eastern Sea with customs pure and plain, fit to restore ancient ways.
units.literal: The Jin arose on the Eastern Sea; its customs were pure and plain, able to return to antiquity.

units.zh: 初入中夏，兵威所加，民多流亡，土多曠閑，遺黎惴惴，何求不獲。
units.en: When they first entered China proper, conquest drove multitudes into exile and left fields fallow; the surviving populace trembled before demands nothing could refuse.
units.literal: When first entering central China, wherever military might reached, many people fled, much land lay idle, survivors trembled—what could they not obtain.

units.zh: 使於斯時，縱不能複井地溝洫之制，若用唐之永業、口分以制民產，仿其租庸調之法以足國計，何至百年之內所為經畫紛紛然，與其國相終始耶！
units.en: Had they then—even without reviving the well-field system—adopted Tang perpetual and equal-field grants to regulate property and Tang-style rent, corvée, and tax to fill the treasury, how could a century of frantic fiscal schemes have dogged the dynasty to its end!
units.literal: If at that time, even if they could not restore the well-field and ditch systems, yet had they used Tang's perpetual and equal-field grants to regulate people's property and imitated its rent, corvée, and tax methods to fill state plans—how would within a century their arrangements have wrangled on, ending only with the state itself!

units.zh: 其弊在於急一時之利，踵久壞之法，及其中葉，鄙遼儉樸，襲宋繁縟之文；
units.en: The fault lay in chasing immediate gain and treading worn-out precedents; by mid-dynasty they scorned Liao thrift yet embraced Song ornament;
units.literal: The abuse lay in hastening short-term profit, following long-broken methods; by the middle period they scorned Liao's thrift and plainness yet adopted Song's ornate culture;

units.zh: 懲宋寬柔，加遼操切之政。
units.en: they rejected Song leniency yet piled on Liao severity.
units.literal: They punished Song's leniency yet added Liao's harshness.

units.zh: 是棄二國之所長，而並用其所短也。
units.en: They discarded each predecessor's strengths and combined its weaknesses.
units.literal: This was abandoning both states' strengths and using both weaknesses together.

units.zh: 繁褥勝必至於傷財，操切勝必至於害民，訖金之世，國用易匱，民心易離，豈不由是歟？
units.en: Ornament exhausts the treasury, severity harms the people—through the Jin age funds ran short and hearts broke away; was the cause not plain?
units.literal: Ornateness prevailing must reach harming wealth; harshness prevailing must reach harming people—through the Jin age state use easily grew scarce and popular hearts easily split; was it not from this?

units.zh: 作法不慎厥初，變法以救其弊，只益甚焉耳。
units.en: Careless lawmaking at the outset and repeated reforms to cure each abuse only deepened the ruin.
units.literal: Making law carelessly at the start, changing law to rescue abuses—only made them worse.

units.zh: 其他鹽策、酒麴、常平、和糴、茶稅、征商、榷場等法，大概多宋舊人之所建明，息耗無定，變易靡恆，視錢鈔何異？
units.en: Salt monopoly, wine tax, ever-normal granaries, state grain purchases, tea duties, transit levies, and frontier markets—mostly Song inheritances—shifted without cease in profit and loss, no steadier than coin and notes.
units.literal: Other salt policies, wine lees, ever-normal granaries, harmonized purchase, tea tax, merchant levies, frontier markets—mostly built on Song predecessors; profit and loss had no fix, change without constancy—as different from coin and notes how?

units.zh: 田制、水利、區田之目，或驟行隨輟，或屢試無效，或熟議未行，鹹著無篇，以備一代之制雲。
units.en: Field regulation, irrigation, and district-field schemes were either rushed then dropped, tried in vain, or debated but never enacted—all noted here without separate chapters to complete the record of the dynasty's institutions.
units.literal: Field systems, water conservancy, district fields—some rushed then stopped, some tried repeatedly without effect, some debated long without enactment—all are recorded without separate chapters to complete the regulations of an age.

units.zh: 金制，男女二歲以下為黃，十五以下為小，十六為中，十七為丁，六十為老，無夫為寡妻妾，諸篤廢疾不為丁。
units.en: Under Jin law, males and females under two sui were infants, under fifteen minors, sixteen youths, seventeen adults liable for service, sixty elderly; widows without husbands included wives and concubines; the seriously ill or disabled were not counted as adults.
units.literal: Jin regulations: males and females under two sui are huang, under fifteen xiao, sixteen zhong, seventeen ding, sixty lao; without a husband gua; wives and concubines; all serious chronic illness not counted as ding.

units.zh: 戶主推其長充，內有物力者為課役戶，無者為不課設戶。
units.en: Household heads nominated their eldest to represent the unit; those with assessed property were corvée households, those without were exempt.
units.literal: Household heads pushed their eldest to serve; those with property within were duty households, without were non-duty households.

units.zh: 令民以五家為保。
units.en: The people were ordered to group themselves in mutual-security units of five households.
units.literal: They ordered the people to form groups of five households as baowu.

units.zh: 泰和六年，上以舊定保伍法，有司滅裂不行，其令結保，有匿奸細、盜賊者連坐。
units.en: In the sixth year of Taihe the emperor noted that the mutual-security law had been slackly enforced and ordered households re-grouped, with collective punishment for concealing spies or bandits.
units.literal: In the sixth year of Taihe, the emperor said the old baowu law was negligently not enforced; he ordered forming baowu; whoever concealed traitors or bandits would suffer collective punishment.

units.zh: 宰臣謂舊以五家為保，恐人易為計構而難覺察，遂令從唐制，五家為鄰、五鄰為保，以相檢察。
units.en: Grand councilors argued that five-household units were too easy to manipulate; the Tang system was adopted—five households a neighborhood, five neighborhoods a security group—for mutual surveillance.
units.literal: Grand councilors said previously five households per baowu—fearing people would easily scheme and be hard to detect—so ordered following Tang: five households neighbor, five neighbors one bao, mutually to inspect.

units.zh: 京府州縣郭下則置坊正，村社則隨戶眾寡為鄉置裏正，以按比戶口，催督賦役，勸課農桑。
units.en: Ward heads were appointed in cities; in villages hamlet heads were set according to population to verify registers, collect taxes, and promote agriculture.
units.literal: In capitals, prefectures, and counties under the walls they set ward heads; in village communities according to household number they set hamlet heads for villages, to compare households, urge levies, encourage farming and sericulture.

units.zh: 村社三百戶以上則設主首四人，二百戶以上三人，五十戶以上二人，以下一人，以佐裏正禁察非違。
units.en: Communities of three hundred households or more had four chief heads, two hundred or more three, fifty or more two, fewer than fifty one—to assist hamlet heads in policing infractions.
units.literal: Village communities of three hundred households and above set four chief heads, two hundred and above three, fifty and above two, below one, to assist hamlet heads in prohibiting and investigating violations.

units.zh: 置壯丁，以佐主首巡警盜賊。
units.en: Strong youths were appointed to help chief heads patrol against bandits.
units.literal: They set strong youths to assist chief heads in patrolling against bandits.

units.zh: 猛安謀克部村寨，五十戶以上設寨使一人，掌同主首。
units.en: In meng'an-mouke villages of fifty households or more one stockade agent was appointed with duties like a chief head.
units.literal: In meng'an mouke tribal villages of fifty households and above one stockade agent was set, duties same as chief head.

units.zh: 寺觀則設綱首。
units.en: Monasteries and temples had their own network heads.
units.literal: Monasteries and temples set network heads.

units.zh: 凡坊正、裏正，以其戶十分內取三分，富民均出顧錢，募強幹有抵保者充，人不得過百貫，役不得過一年。
units.en: Ward and hamlet heads were drawn from three in ten households; wealthy families shared hire costs to recruit capable men with guarantors; pay was capped at one hundred strings and tenure at one year.
units.literal: For ward and hamlet heads, from their households' ten parts took three parts; wealthy households equally paid hire money, recruiting strong capable men with collateral guarantees; no person over one hundred strings, service not over one year.

units.zh: 大定二十九年，章宗嘗欲罷坊、裏正，複以主首遠，入城應代，妨農不便，乃以有物力謹願者二年一更代。
units.en: In the twenty-ninth year of Dading Zhangzong considered abolishing ward and hamlet heads; travel to town for duty harmed farming, so property-holding prudent men were rotated every two years.
units.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Dading, Zhangzong once wished to abolish ward and hamlet heads; again because chief heads were distant, entering the city for corvée harmed farming and was inconvenient, so those with property and prudent character served two-year rotations.

units.zh: 凡戶口計帳，三年一籍。
units.en: Household registers were revised every three years.
units.literal: All household registers and account books—once every three years.

units.zh: 自正月初，州縣以裏正、主首，猛安謀克則以寨使，詣編戶家責手實，具男女老幼年與姓名，生者增之，死者除之。
units.en: From the first day of the first month, counties sent hamlet and chief heads—meng'an-mouke units sent stockade agents—to demand household statements listing every person by age and name, adding births and striking the dead.
units.literal: From the first day of the first month, prefectures and counties with hamlet heads and chief heads; meng'an mouke with stockade agents—visiting registered households demanding household statements, listing males and females old and young with names; born added, dead removed.

units.zh: 正月二十日以實數報縣，二月二十日申州，以十日內達上司，無遠近皆以四月二十日到部呈省。
units.en: True counts reached the county by the twentieth of the first month, the prefecture by the twentieth of the second, superiors within ten days thereafter, and the ministry by the twentieth of the fourth month regardless of distance.
units.literal: By the twentieth day of the first month report truth to the county; by the twentieth of the second month report to the prefecture, within ten days reach the superior; regardless of distance all reach the ministry by the twentieth of the fourth month presenting to the province.

units.zh: 凡漢人、渤海人不得充猛安謀克戶。
units.en: Han Chinese and Bohai people could not register as meng'an-mouke households.
units.literal: All Han Chinese and Bohai people could not become meng'an mouke households.

units.zh: 猛安謀克之奴婢免為良者，止隸本部為正戶。
units.en: Bondservants of meng'an-mouke units who were freed remained attached to their original unit as regular households.
units.literal: Slaves of meng'an mouke freed to commoner status only attached to the original unit as regular households.

units.zh: 凡沒入官良人，隸宮籍監為監戶，沒入官奴婢，隸太府監為官戶。
units.en: Free persons confiscated by the state were registered under the palace registry as supervised households; confiscated slaves under the imperial treasury as official households.
units.literal: All free persons confiscated to government attached to the palace registry as supervised households; confiscated slaves attached to the imperial treasury as official households.

units.zh: 當收國二年時，法制未定，兵革未息，貧民多依權右為苟安，多隱蔽為奴婢者。
units.en: In the second year of Shouguo institutions were unsettled and war unceasing; the poor clung to powerful patrons and many concealed themselves as bond slaves.
units.literal: In the second year of Shouguo, legal institutions were unsettled, warfare not ceased, poor people mostly relied on powerful families for temporary safety, many hid as slave bondservants.

units.zh: 太祖下詔曰：「比以歲凶民饑，多附豪族，因陷為奴隸。
units.en: Taizu decreed: "Of late famine has driven the people to attach themselves to great clans and fall into slavery.
units.literal: Taizu issued an edict saying: "Recently because years were bad the people starved, many attached to great clans and thereby fell into slavery.

units.zh: 及有犯法，征償莫辦，折身為奴。
units.en: Some who broke the law, unable to pay fines, forfeited their persons as slaves.
units.literal: When some broke the law and could not pay compensation, they forfeited their bodies to become slaves.

units.zh: 或私約立限，以人對贖，過期則以為奴者。
units.en: Others made private contracts pledging persons as ransom—when the term expired they became slaves.
units.literal: Or privately set term contracts, redeeming with persons—when the term expired they became slaves.

units.zh: 並聽以兩人贖一為良，元約以一人贖者從便。」
units.en: All were allowed to redeem one bondservant as free with two persons; where the original contract was one for one, that term stood."
units.literal: All were permitted to redeem one as free person with two persons; original contracts of one for one followed convenience."

units.zh: 天輔五年，以境土既拓，而舊部多瘠鹵，將移其民於泰州，乃遣皇弟昱及族子宗雄按視其地。
units.en: In the fifth year of Tianfu, with territory expanded but old domains mostly barren, the court planned to relocate people to Taizhou and sent the emperor's younger brother Yu and clansman Zongxiong to survey the land.
units.literal: In the fifth year of Tianfu, territory already expanded while old territories mostly saline and poor, about to move the people to Taizhou—sent the imperial younger brother Yu and clansman Zongxiong to inspect the land.

units.zh: 昱等苴其土以進，言可種植，遂摘諸猛安謀克中民戶萬余，使宗人婆盧火統之，屯種於泰州。
units.en: Yu and his party brought samples of the soil, reported it arable, and selected more than ten thousand civilian households from meng'an-mouke units under clansman Boluohuo to farm at Taizhou.
units.literal: Yu and others wrapped the soil and presented it, saying it could be planted; they then selected more than ten thousand civilian households from the meng'an mouke, had clansman Boluohuo command them, and settled them to farm at Taizhou.

units.zh: 婆廬火舊居阿注滸水又作按出虎，至是遷焉。
units.en: Boluohuo, who had lived on the Azhu River (also written Anchuhu), moved there at this time.
units.literal: Boluohuo formerly dwelt at the Azhu River, also written Anchuhu; at this time he moved there.

units.zh: 其居甯江州者，遣拾得、查端、阿裏徒歡、奚撻罕等四謀克，挈家屬耕具，徙於泰州，仍賜婆盧火耕牛五十。
units.en: Four mouke led by Shide, Chaduan, Alituhuan, and Xitahan were sent from Ningjiang with families and tools to Taizhou, and Boluohuo was given fifty plow oxen.
units.literal: Those dwelling at Ningjiang Prefecture—sent Shide, Chaduan, Alituhuan, Xitahan and four mouke, bringing families and farm tools, moved to Taizhou, and still granted Boluohuo fifty plow oxen.

units.zh: 天輔六年，既定山西諸州，以上京為內地，則移其民實之。
units.en: In the sixth year of Tianfu, after pacifying Shanxi, the court made the Upper Capital the inner core and relocated people to populate it.
units.literal: In the sixth year of Tianfu, having pacified the Shanxi prefectures, with the Upper Capital as inner territory, they moved the people to fill it.

units.zh: 又命耶律佛頂以兵護送諸降人于渾河路，以皇弟昂監之，命從便以居。
units.en: Yelü Foding was ordered to escort surrendered peoples along the Hun River route under the emperor's younger brother Ang, who let them settle where convenient.
units.literal: They also ordered Yelü Foding to escort surrendered people with troops on the Hun River route, with the imperial younger brother Ang supervising, ordering them to settle as convenient.

units.zh: 七年，以山西諸部族近西北二邊，且遼主未獲，恐陰相結誘，複命皇弟昂與孛堇稍喝等以兵四千護送，處之嶺東，惟西京民安堵如故，且命昂鎮守上京路。
units.en: In the seventh year, fearing Shanxi tribes near the northwest frontiers might ally with the uncaptured Liao ruler, Ang and Chief Shaohe escorted them east of the mountains with four thousand troops; Western Capital was left undisturbed and Ang garrisoned the Upper Capital route.
units.literal: In the seventh year, because Shanxi tribal groups were near the two northwest frontiers and the Liao ruler had not been captured, fearing secret collusion and enticement, they again ordered the imperial younger brother Ang with Chief Shaohe and others to escort with four thousand troops, placing them east of the mountains; only Western Capital people remained settled as before, and Ang was ordered to guard the Upper Capital route.

units.zh: 既而，上聞昂已過上京，而降人複苦其侵擾多叛亡者，遂命孛堇出裏底往戒諭之，比至，而諸部已叛去。
units.en: Learning that Ang had passed the Upper Capital while harassing surrendered peoples into revolt, the court sent Chief Chulidi to admonish him—but the tribes had already fled by his arrival.
units.literal: Then the emperor heard Ang had passed the Upper Capital, while surrendered people again suffered his harassment and many rebelled and fled; he ordered Chief Chulidi to go admonish them, but by the time he arrived the tribes had already rebelled and left.

units.zh: 又以猛安詳穩留住所領歸附之民還東京，命有司常撫慰，且貸一歲之糧，其親屬被虜者皆令聚居。
units.en: Meng'an xiangwen Liuzhu was sent to bring his submitted followers back to the Eastern Capital; officials were to comfort them, grant a year's grain, and reunite families separated by capture.
units.literal: They also had meng'an xiangwen Liuzhu lead the submitted people he commanded back to the Eastern Capital, ordered officials constantly to comfort them, and loaned one year's grain; those whose kin had been captured were all ordered to settle together.

units.zh: 及七年取燕京路，二月，盡徙六州氏族富強工技之民於內地。
units.en: When the Yanjing region fell in the seventh year, the court in the second month relocated all wealthy clans and skilled artisans of the six prefectures inland.
units.literal: When in the seventh year they took the Yanjing route, in the second month they moved all clans, the strong, and skilled craftsmen of the six prefectures to the inner territories.

units.zh: 太宗天會元年，以舊徙潤、隰等四州之民于沈州之境，以新遷之戶艱苦不能自存，詔曰：「比聞民乏食至鬻子者，聽以丁力等者贖之。」
units.en: In Taizong's first year of Tianhui, settlers moved from Run, Xi, and four other prefectures to Shenzhou were starving; the court decreed: "Hearing that the people lack food to the point of selling children, permit redeeming them with labor of equal value."
units.literal: In the first year of Tianhui under Taizong, because people formerly moved from Run, Xi and four other prefectures to Shenzhou territory, and newly relocated households suffered hardship and could not support themselves, an edict said: "Recently we hear the people lack food to the point of selling children; permit redeeming them with labor of equal value."

units.zh: 又詔孛堇阿實賚曰：「先皇帝以同姓之人昔有自鬻及典質其身者，命官為贖。
units.en: Chief Ashilai was also instructed: "The late emperor ordered officials to redeem clansmen who had sold or pawned themselves.
units.literal: They also decreed to Chief Ashilai: "The former emperor, because persons of the same surname had formerly sold themselves or pawned their bodies, ordered officials to redeem them.

units.zh: 今聞尚有未複者，其悉閱贖之。」
units.en: We hear some remain unredeemed—review every case and redeem them."
units.literal: Now we hear there are still some not restored; thoroughly review and redeem them all."

units.zh: 又命以官粟贖上京路新遷置甯江州戶口貧而賣身者，六百餘人。
units.en: Official grain was used to redeem more than six hundred poor settlers on the Upper Capital route who had sold themselves into bondage.
units.literal: They also ordered using official grain to redeem on the Upper Capital route newly relocated Ningjiang Prefecture households who were poor and sold their persons—more than six hundred people.

units.zh: 二年，民有自鬻為奴者，詔以丁力等者易之。
units.en: In the second year, self-sale into slavery was met with orders to exchange bondservants for labor of equal value.
units.literal: In the second year, when people sold themselves as slaves, an edict ordered exchanging them with labor of equal value.

units.zh: 三年，禁內外官及宗室毋得私役百姓，權勢家不得買貧民為奴，其脅買者一人償十五人，詐買者一人償二人，罪皆杖百。
units.en: In the third year, officials and imperial kin were forbidden to press commoners into private service; powerful families could not buy the poor as slaves—coerced purchases required fifteen replacements, fraudulent ones two, all punished with a hundred strokes.
units.literal: In the third year, they forbade inner and outer officials and the imperial clan from privately employing commoners; powerful families could not buy poor people as slaves; coerced buyers compensated one for fifteen persons, fraudulent buyers one for two persons; all crimes punished with one hundred strokes.

units.zh: 七年，詔兵興以來，良人被略為驅者，聽其父母妻子贖之。
units.en: In the seventh year, free persons seized as bond servants since the wars began were permitted redemption by parents, wives, or children.
units.literal: In the seventh year, an edict said since warfare arose, free persons seized as bond servants—permit their parents, wives, and children to redeem them.

units.zh: 熙宗皇統四年詔陝西、蒲、解、汝、蔡等州歲饑，百姓流落典雇為驅者，官以絹贖為良，丁男三匹，婦人幼小二匹。
units.en: In Xizong's fourth year of Huangtong, famine in Shaanxi, Pu, Jie, Ru, Cai, and other prefectures drove people to pawn themselves as bond servants; the state redeemed them with silk—three bolts for adult men, two for women and children.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Huangtong under Xizong, an edict said Shaanxi, Pu, Jie, Ru, Cai and other prefectures had yearly famine; commoners drifting about pawned or hired out as bond servants—the government redeemed them as free with silk, three bolts for adult males, two bolts for women and small children.

units.zh: 世宗大定二年，詔免二稅戶為民。
units.en: In Shizong's second year of Dading, double-tax households were freed as commoners.
units.literal: In the second year of Dading under Shizong, an edict freed double-tax households as commoners.

units.zh: 初，遼人佞佛尤甚，多以良民賜諸寺，分其稅一半輸官，一半輸寺，故謂之二稅戶。
units.en: Under Liao, devotion to Buddhism led many free commoners to be granted to temples, paying tax half to the state and half to the monastery—hence the name double-tax households.
units.literal: At first, Liao people were especially devoted to Buddhism; many free commoners were granted to monasteries, their tax half paid to government, half to the monastery—hence called double-tax households.

units.zh: 遼亡，僧多匿其實，抑為賤，有援佐證以告者，有司各執以聞，上素知其事，故特免之。
units.en: After Liao fell, monks often concealed the truth and kept them in servile status; petitioners with evidence were heard by each office; the emperor, long aware, specially freed them.
units.literal: When Liao perished, monks mostly concealed the facts and kept them as lowly; those with supporting evidence who reported—each office held and reported; the emperor long knew this matter, so specially freed them.

units.zh: 十七年五月，省奏：「咸平府路一千六百餘戶，自陳皆長白山星顯、禪春河女直人，遼時簽為獵戶，移居于此，號移典部，遂附契丹籍。
units.en: In the fifth month of the seventeenth year the province reported: "More than 1,600 households on the Xianping route claimed to be Jurchen from Changbai Mountain and the Chanchun River, enrolled under Liao as hunter households, relocated here as the Yidian tribe, and registered as Khitan subjects.
units.literal: In the fifth month of the seventeenth year, the province reported: "More than 1,600 households on the Xianping route circuit state they are all Jurchen of Changbai Mountain Xingxian and Chanchun River; in Liao times enrolled as hunter households, moved here, called the Yidian tribe, and attached to Khitan registers.

units.zh: 本朝義兵之興，首詣軍降，仍居本部，今乞厘正。」
units.en: When our armies rose they were among the first to surrender and remained in their original units; they now ask to have their status corrected."
units.literal: When our dynasty's righteous armies arose, they first came to the army to surrender and still dwelt in their original units; now they beg rectification."

units.zh: 詔從之。
units.en: The court approved their request.
units.literal: An edict approved it.

units.zh: 二十年，以上京路女直人戶，規避物力，自賣其奴婢，致耕田者少，遂以貧乏，詔定制禁之。
units.en: In the twentieth year, Jurchen households on the Upper Capital route evaded property tax by selling bondsmen, leaving too few to farm and causing poverty; regulations were issued to forbid the practice.
units.literal: In the twentieth year, because Jurchen households on the Upper Capital route evaded property assessment by selling their slaves and bondservants, causing few to till fields and thus poverty, an edict fixed regulations forbidding it.

units.zh: 又謂宰臣曰：「猛安謀克人戶，兄弟親屬若各隨所分土，與漢人錯居，每四五十戶結為保聚，農作時令相助濟，此亦勸相之道也。」
units.en: He told the grand councilors: "If meng'an-mouke kin settle on allotted lands among Han neighbors in clusters of forty or fifty households, aiding one another at planting and harvest, that too is mutual encouragement."
units.literal: He also told grand councilors: "Meng'an mouke households—if brothers and kin each follow their allotted land and live intermixed with Han Chinese, every forty or fifty households forming a security cluster, helping one another in farming seasons—this too is the way of encouraging mutual aid."

units.zh: 二十一年六月，徙銀山側民於臨潢。
units.en: In the sixth month of the twenty-first year, people from the Yinshan slopes were moved to Linhuang.
units.literal: In the sixth month of the twenty-first year, they moved people from the Yinshan slopes to Linhuang.

units.zh: 又命避役之戶舉家逃於他所者，元貫及所寓司縣官同罪，為定制。
units.en: Households fleeing corvée with whole families were ordered punished together with their original registration and host county officials—a fixed regulation.
units.literal: They also ordered that households evading corvée who fled with whole families elsewhere—their original registration and the officials of the host prefecture or county shared guilt; this became fixed regulation.

units.zh: 二十三年，定制，女直奴婢如有得力，本主許令婚娉者，須取問房親及村老給據，方許娉於良人。
units.en: In the twenty-third year it was regulated that capable Jurchen bondwomen permitted to marry by their masters required kin and village-elder certificates before marrying free men.
units.literal: In the twenty-third year, regulations fixed: if Jurchen slave women were capable, and the master permitted marriage, they must inquire of kin and village elders for certificates before permitting marriage to free persons.

units.zh: 是年八月，奏猛安謀克戶口、墾地、牛具之數。
units.en: That August, meng'an-mouke household counts, reclaimed land, and ox teams were reported.
units.literal: In the eighth month of that year, they reported meng'an mouke household counts, reclaimed land, and ox-team numbers.

units.zh: 猛安二百二，謀克千八百七十八，戶六十一萬五千六百二十四，口六百一十五萬八千六百三十六，內正口四百八十一萬二千六百六十九，奴婢口一百三十四萬五千九百六十七。
units.en: There were 202 meng'an, 1,878 mouke, 615,624 households, and 6,158,636 persons—including 4,812,669 free persons and 1,345,967 bond servants.
units.literal: Meng'an 202, mouke 1,878, households 615,624, persons 6,158,636, of which regular persons 4,812,669, slave persons 1,345,967.

units.zh: 墾田一百六十九萬三百八十頃有奇，牛具三十八萬四千七百七十一。
units.en: Reclaimed land totaled more than 1,690,380 qing, with 384,771 ox teams.
units.literal: Reclaimed fields 1,690,380-odd qing, ox teams 384,771.

units.zh: 在都宗室將軍司，戶一百七十，口二萬八千七百九十，內正口九百八十二，奴婢口二萬七千八百八。
units.en: The Capital Imperial Clan General Office had 170 households and 28,790 persons—982 free and 27,808 bond.
units.literal: Capital Imperial Clan General Office: households 170, persons 28,790, of which regular 982, slave 27,808.

units.zh: 墾田三千六百八十三頃七十五畝，牛具三百四。
units.en: It held 3,683 qing 75 mu of reclaimed land and 304 ox teams.
units.literal: Reclaimed fields 3,683 qing 75 mu, ox teams 304.

units.zh: 迭剌、唐西二部五颭，戶五千五百八十五，口十三萬七千五百四十四，內正口十一萬九千四百六十三，奴婢口一萬八千八十一。
units.en: The Diela and Tangxi divisions' five banners had 5,585 households and 137,544 persons—119,463 free and 18,081 bond.
units.literal: Diela and Tangxi two divisions five banners: households 5,585, persons 137,544, of which regular 119,463, slave 18,081.

units.zh: 墾田萬六千二十四頃一十七畝，牛具五千六十六。
units.en: They held 16,024 qing 17 mu of reclaimed land and 5,066 ox teams.
units.literal: Reclaimed fields 16,024 qing 17 mu, ox teams 5,066.

units.zh: 二十五年，命宰臣禁有祿人一子、及農民避課役，為僧道者。
units.en: In the twenty-fifth year, officials were ordered to forbid salaried officials' sons and farmers evading corvée from taking monastic orders.
units.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, grand councilors were ordered to forbid salaried officials' sons and farmers evading corvée from becoming monks or Daoists.

units.zh: 大定初，天下戶才三百余萬，至二十七年天下戶六百七十八萬九千四百四十九，口四千四百七十萬五千八十六。
units.en: At the start of Dading the empire had barely three million households; by the twenty-seventh year it had 6,789,449 households and 44,705,086 persons.
units.literal: At the beginning of Dading, empire-wide households were only a little over three million; by the twenty-seventh year empire-wide households were 6,789,449, persons 44,705,086.

units.zh: 章宗大定二十九年十一月，上封事者言，乞放二稅戶為良。
units.en: In the eleventh month of Zhangzong's twenty-ninth year of Dading, a memorialist asked to free double-tax households.
units.literal: In the eleventh month of the twenty-ninth year of Dading under Zhangzong, a memorialist asked to release double-tax households as free persons.

units.zh: 省臣欲取公牒可憑者為准，參知政事移剌履謂：「憑驗真偽難明，凡契丹奴婢今後所生者悉為良，見有者則不得典賣，如此則三十年後奴皆為良，而民且不病焉。」
units.en: Provincial ministers wanted documentary proof; Vice Grand Councilor Yelü Lü said: "Verification of truth and falsehood is hard to clarify; all Khitan bond servants born hereafter should be free, existing ones not pawned or sold—in thirty years all would be free without harming the people."
units.literal: Provincial ministers wished to take verifiable official documents as standard; Vice Grand Councilor Yelü Lü said: "Verification of truth and falsehood is hard to clarify; all Khitan slaves born hereafter shall be free; existing ones may not be pawned or sold—thus in thirty years all slaves will be free and the people will not suffer."

units.zh: 上以履言未當，令再議。
units.en: The emperor found Lü's proposal unsatisfactory and ordered further debate.
units.literal: The emperor said Lü's words were not appropriate and ordered further discussion.

units.zh: 省奏謂不拘括則訟終不絕，遂遣大興府治中烏古孫仲和、侍御史范楫分括北京路及中都路二稅戶，凡無憑驗，其主自言之者及因通檢而知之者，其稅半輸官，半輸主，而有憑驗者悉放為良。
units.en: The province warned that without investigation lawsuits would never end; Wugusun Zhonghe and Fan Ji were sent to investigate double-tax households on the Beijing and Central Capital routes—unverified cases where masters confessed or comprehensive inspection revealed them paid tax half to state and half to master; verified cases were all freed.
units.literal: The province reported that without investigation lawsuits would never end; they sent Daxing Prefecture Administrator Wugusun Zhonghe and Attending Censor Fan Ji to investigate double-tax households on the Beijing route and Central Capital route separately; all without verification—those whose masters spoke themselves or were known through comprehensive inspection—half tax to government, half to master; those with verification all released as free.

units.zh: 明昌元年正月，上封事者言：「自古以農桑為本，今商賈之外又有佛、老與他遊食，浮費百倍。
units.en: In the first month of Mingchang a memorialist said: "Since antiquity agriculture has been the foundation; beyond merchants, Buddhism, Daoism, and other wandering livelihoods now consume a hundredfold in waste.
units.literal: In the first month of the first year of Mingchang, a memorialist said: "From antiquity farming and sericulture were the foundation; now beyond merchants there are also Buddhism, Daoism, and other wandering livelihoods, extravagant expenses a hundredfold.

units.zh: 農歲不登，流殍相望，此末作傷農者多故也。」
units.en: When harvests fail, refugees and corpses line the roads—chiefly because secondary pursuits drain agriculture."
units.literal: When farming years fail, refugees and corpses face one another—this has many causes in secondary pursuits harming agriculture."

units.zh: 上乃下令，禁自披剃為僧、道者。
units.en: The emperor then forbade self-initiation as monk or Daoist priest.
units.literal: The emperor then issued orders forbidding self-tonsure as monk or Daoist.

units.zh: 是歲，奏天下戶六百九十三萬九千，口四千五百四十四萬七千九百，而粟止五千二百二十六萬一千余石，除官兵二年之費，余驗口計之，口月食五鬥，可為四十四日之食。
units.en: That year the empire had 6,939,000 households and 45,447,900 persons, but only 52,261,000-odd shi of grain—after two years' military and official consumption, at five dou per person per month, enough for forty-four days.
units.literal: That year they reported empire-wide households 6,939,000, persons 45,447,900, while grain was only 52,261,000-odd shi; deducting two years' expenses for troops and officials, checking by persons, each person five dou monthly—could supply forty-four days' food.

units.zh: 上曰：「蓄積不多，是力農者少故也。
units.en: The emperor said: "Reserves are scant because too few labor at farming.
units.literal: The emperor said: "Stored reserves are not abundant—this is because those laboring in farming are few.

units.zh: 其集百官，議所以使民務本廣儲之道，以聞。」
units.en: He ordered officials to discuss how to make the people attend to fundamentals and build reserves, and report back."
units.literal: Gather the hundred officials to discuss ways to make the people attend to fundamentals and broaden stores, and report."

units.zh: 六月，奏北京等路所免二稅戶，凡一千七百余戶，萬三千九百餘口，此後為良為驅，皆從已斷為定。
units.en: In the sixth month it was reported that more than 1,700 households and 13,900 persons on the Beijing route and elsewhere were freed as double-tax households; thereafter free or bond status followed prior rulings.
units.literal: In the sixth month, they reported on the Beijing route and others freed double-tax households—altogether more than 1,700 households, more than 13,900 persons; thereafter whether free or bond, all followed prior judgments as fixed.

units.zh: 明昌六年二月，上謂宰臣曰：「凡言女直進士，不須稱女直字。
units.en: In the second month of Mingchang's sixth year the emperor told councilors: "When speaking of Jurchen jinshi graduates, do not use the word Jurchen.
units.literal: In the second month of the sixth year of Mingchang, the emperor told grand councilors: "Whenever speaking of Jurchen jinshi, do not use the word Jurchen.

units.zh: 卿等誤作回避女直、契丹語，非也。
units.en: You mistake this for avoiding Jurchen and Khitan terms—that is wrong.
units.literal: You mistakenly treat it as avoiding Jurchen and Khitan language—this is wrong.

units.zh: 今如分別戶民，則女直言本戶，漢戶及契丹，餘謂之雜戶。」
units.en: In distinguishing household types, Jurchen are original households, Han and Khitan are separate, and the rest are miscellaneous households."
units.literal: Now if distinguishing household peoples, Jurchen are called original households, Han and Khitan, the rest called miscellaneous households."

units.zh: 明昌六年十二月，奏天下女直、契丹、漢戶七百二十二萬三千四百，口四千八百四十九萬四百，物力錢二百六十萬四千七百四十二貫。
units.en: In the twelfth month of Mingchang's sixth year the empire reported 7,223,400 Jurchen, Khitan, and Han households, 48,490,400 persons, and 2,604,742 strings in property assessments.
units.literal: In the twelfth month of the sixth year of Mingchang, they reported empire-wide Jurchen, Khitan, and Han households 7,223,400, persons 48,490,400, property assessment money 2,604,742 strings.

units.zh: 泰和七年六月，敕，中物力戶，有役則多逃避，有司令以次戶代之，事畢則複業，以致大損不逃之戶。
units.en: In the sixth month of Taihe's seventh year, middle property households often evaded corvée; officials substituted lower households, who resumed after duty—greatly harming those who did not flee.
units.literal: In the sixth month of the seventh year of Taihe, an edict said middle property-assessment households, when there was corvée mostly evaded; officials ordered lower households to substitute; when affairs ended they resumed business, greatly harming households that did not flee.

units.zh: 令省臣詳議。
units.en: Provincial ministers were ordered to deliberate.
units.literal: Order provincial ministers to discuss in detail.

units.zh: 宰臣奏：「舊制太輕。」
units.en: Grand councilors reported: "The old penalties were too light."
units.literal: Grand councilors reported: "The old regulations are too light."

units.zh: 遂命課役全戶逃者徒二年，賞告者錢五萬。
units.en: Full corvée households who fled were sentenced to two years' penal servitude and informers rewarded fifty thousand cash.
units.literal: They then ordered full corvée households who fled to penal servitude two years, reward informers fifty thousand cash.

units.zh: 先逃者以百日內自首，免罪。
units.en: Prior fugitives who surrendered within a hundred days were pardoned.
units.literal: Prior fugitives who surrendered within a hundred days were exempted from punishment.

units.zh: 如實銷乏者，內從禦史台，外從按察司，體究免之。
units.en: Those truly bankrupt were to be investigated and exempted by the Censorate within and surveillance commissioners without.
units.literal: If truly bankrupt, inner from the Censorate, outer from surveillance commissioners—investigate and exempt.

units.zh: 十二月，奏天下戶七百六十八萬四千四百三十八，口四千五百八十一萬六千七十九。
units.en: In the twelfth month the empire reported 7,684,438 households and 45,816,079 persons.
units.literal: In the twelfth month, they reported empire-wide households 7,684,438, persons 45,816,079.

units.zh: 戶增於大定二十七年一百六十二萬三千七百一十五，口增八百八十二萬七千六十五。
units.en: Households had risen by 1,623,715 and persons by 8,827,065 since Dading's twenty-seventh year.
units.literal: Households increased from the twenty-seventh year of Dading by 1,623,715; persons increased by 8,827,065.

units.zh: 此金版籍之極盛也。
units.en: This was the peak of Jin population registers.
units.literal: This was the Jin register's greatest flourishing.

units.zh: 及衛紹王之時，軍旅不息，宣宗立而南遷，死徙之餘，所在為虛矣。
units.en: During the reign of Weishao Wang, warfare never ceased; after Xuanzong's accession and southern move, death and flight left regions depopulated.
units.literal: During the time of Weishao Wang, armies and campaigns never ceased; when Xuanzong came to the throne and moved south, after deaths and flight the places everywhere were empty.

units.zh: 戶口日耗，軍費日急，賦斂繁重，皆仰給于河南，民不堪命，率棄廬田，相繼亡去。
units.en: Population dwindled daily as military costs mounted and levies grew crushing—all support fell on Henan; people could not endure it, abandoned homesteads, and fled in succession.
units.literal: Household registers daily dwindled, military expenses daily grew urgent, levies and collections were heavy—all relied on supplies from Henan; the people could not bear the burden, mostly abandoning their homestead fields and fleeing one after another.

units.zh: 及屢降詔招複業者，免其歲之租，然以國用乏竭，逃者之租皆令居者代出，以故多不敢還。
units.en: Repeated edicts offered fleeing farmers rent amnesty to return, but state coffers were empty—absentees' taxes were charged to those who stayed, so many dared not come back.
units.literal: When edicts repeatedly summoned those who had fled to return to farming, their year's rent was waived, yet because state funds were exhausted, the rent of those who fled was all ordered paid by those who remained, for which reason many dared not return.

units.zh: 興定元年十二月，宣宗欲懸賞募人捕亡戶，而複慮騷動，遂命依已降詔書，已免債逋，更招一月，違而不來者然後捕獲治罪，而以所遺地賜人。
units.en: In the twelfth month of Xingding 1, Xuanzong wanted bounties to catch absent households but feared unrest; he ordered following prior edicts—debts forgiven, one more month to return, then capture and punish holdouts and grant their abandoned land to others.
units.literal: In the twelfth month of the first year of Xingding, Xuanzong wished to offer rewards to recruit men to capture absent households, yet again feared disturbance; he therefore ordered accordance with already issued edicts—already forgiven debts and arrears, summon again for one month, and only after those who violated and did not come were then captured and punished, while abandoned land was granted to others.

units.zh: 四年，省臣奏：「河南以歲饑而賦役不息，所亡戶令有司招之，至明年三月不復業者，論如律。」
units.en: In the fourth year provincial ministers reported: "Henan suffers famine yet levies continue; absent households must be summoned, and those who have not resumed farming by the third month of the following year shall be punished by law."
units.literal: In the fourth year, provincial ministers reported: "Henan, with famine this year, yet levies and corvée cease not; absent households are ordered recruited by the responsible offices; those who have not returned to farming by the third month of next year are to be handled according to law."

units.zh: 時河壖為疆，烽鞞屢警，故集慶軍節度使溫蒂罕達言：「亳州戶舊六萬，自南遷以來，不勝調發，相繼逃去，所存者曾無十一，碭山下邑，野無居民矣！」
units.en: With the river frontier under alert and beacons firing, Jiqing Army Military Commissioner Wendihanda said: "Bozhou once had sixty thousand households; since the southern withdrawal they could not bear the levies and fled—fewer than one in ten remain; below the Dang Mountains the countryside is deserted!"
units.literal: At that time the river embankments were the frontier; beacon signals and drums repeatedly alerted; therefore Jiqing Army Military Commissioner Wen Ti Han Da said: "Bozhou households once numbered sixty thousand; since the southern move, unable to bear mobilizations, they fled in succession—of those who remain not even one in ten; below the Dang Mountains the county towns in the countryside have no inhabitants!"

units.zh: 通檢推排
units.en: Comprehensive Inspection and Reorganization by Assessment
units.literal: Comprehensive Inspection and Reorganization by Assessment

units.zh: 通檢，即《周禮》大司徒三年一大比，各登其鄉之眾寡、六畜、車輦，辨物行征之制也。
units.en: Comprehensive inspection follows the Rites of Zhou: every three years the Grand Minister of Education took a great census, registering each district's population, livestock, and vehicles—the system for distinguishing goods and levying duties.
units.literal: Comprehensive inspection is the Rites of Zhou Grand Minister of Education's great comparison every three years, each registering his district's numbers, six livestock, carriages and teams—the system of distinguishing goods and levying transit duties.

units.zh: 金自國初占籍之後，至大定四年，承正隆師旅之餘，民之貧富變更，賦役不均，世宗下詔曰：「粵自國初，有司常行大比，於今四十年矣。
units.en: From the dynasty's founding registers to the fourth year of Dading, after Zhenglong's wars wealth and poverty had shifted and levies grown uneven; Shizong decreed: "Since the founding, officials have held great censuses—forty years have passed.
units.literal: From the Jin's initial occupation of registers after the founding, to the fourth year of Dading, inheriting the aftermath of Zhenglong armies, the people's rich and poor changed, levies and corvée uneven; Shizong issued an edict: "Since the founding, officials regularly conducted great comparisons—it has been forty years now.

units.zh: 正隆時，兵役並興，調發無度，富者今貧不能自存，版籍所無者今為富室而猶倖免。
units.en: Under Zhenglong, armies mobilized without limit—the once rich now could not survive, while the unregistered grew wealthy yet still escaped duty.
units.literal: In Zhenglong times military service arose together, mobilization without measure; the rich are now poor and cannot support themselves, those absent from registers are now wealthy houses yet still escape by luck.

units.zh: 是用遣信臣泰甯軍節度使張弘信等十三人，分路通檢天下物力而差定之，以革前弊，俾元元無不均之歎，以稱朕意。
units.en: Thirteen trusted envoys led by Taining Army Commissioner Zhang Hongxin were sent on separate routes to inspect property empire-wide and fix gradations, reform abuses, and spare the people uneven burdens—as the emperor intended.
units.literal: Therefore trusted ministers were sent—Taining Army Commissioner Zhang Hongxin and thirteen others—to conduct comprehensive inspection of empire-wide property by route and fix gradations, to reform prior abuses, so the masses have no uneven lament, matching Our intent.

units.zh: 凡規措條理，命尚書省畫一以行。」
units.en: All arrangements were ordered unified and implemented through the Ministry of Revenue."
units.literal: All planning arrangements and regulations—the Ministry of Revenue was ordered to unify and implement."

units.zh: 又命：「凡監戶事產，除官所撥賜之外，餘凡置到百姓有稅田宅。
units.en: It was also ordered: "All supervised households' property, beyond official grants, and any taxable land or houses commoners acquired,
units.literal: They also ordered: "All supervised households' estates—apart from what officials granted—whatever commoners acquired with taxable fields and houses,

units.zh: 皆在通檢之數。」
units.en: all fell within the comprehensive inspection."
units.literal: all fall within comprehensive inspection's count."

units.zh: 時諸使往往以苛酷多得物力為功，弘信檢山東州縣尤為酷暴，棣州防禦使完顏永元面責之曰：「朝廷以正隆後差調不均，故命使者均之。
units.en: Envoys often treated harshness and inflated assessments as merit; Hongxin's inspection of Shandong was especially brutal; Di Prefecture Defense Commissioner Wanyan Yongyuan rebuked him: "The court sent you to equalize burdens after Zhenglong's uneven levies.
units.literal: At the time envoys often took harsh severity and gaining much property assessment as merit; Hongxin inspecting Shandong prefectures and counties was especially cruel and violent; Di Prefecture Defense Commissioner Wanyan Yongyuan rebuked him to his face: "The court, because after Zhenglong corvée assignments were uneven, ordered envoys to equalize them.

units.zh: 今乃殘暴，妄加民產業數倍，一有來申訴者，則血肉淋離，甚者即殞杖下，此何理也？」
units.en: Instead you brutalize the people, multiplying assessments severalfold; appellants are beaten until flesh tears and some die under the rod—what justice is this?"
units.literal: Now you are brutal and violent, recklessly multiplying people's estates several fold; whenever someone came to appeal, flesh and blood were torn streaming; the severe even died under the staff—what principle is this?"

units.zh: 弘信不能對，故惟棣州稍平。
units.en: Hongxin had no answer; only Di Prefecture remained relatively calm.
units.literal: Hongxin could not reply; therefore only Di Prefecture was somewhat calm.

units.zh: 五年，有司奏諸路通檢不均，詔再以戶口多寡、貧富輕重，適中定之。
units.en: In the fifth year, uneven inspection across routes was reported; the court re-fixed gradations by household size and wealth.
units.literal: In the fifth year, offices reported routes' comprehensive inspection uneven; an edict again fixed by household numbers, rich and poor, light and heavy—moderately determined.

units.zh: 既而，又定通檢地土等第稅法。
units.en: Land grades and tax rates for comprehensive inspection were then fixed.
units.literal: Then they also fixed comprehensive inspection land grades and tax law.

units.zh: 十五年九月，上以天下物力，自通檢以來十餘年，貧富變易，賦調輕重不均，遣濟南尹梁肅等二十六人，分路推排。
units.en: In the ninth month of the fifteenth year, noting that wealth had shifted in the decade since comprehensive inspection and levies grown uneven, the emperor sent Jinan Prefect Liang Su and twenty-six others on separate routes to reassess and re-rank property.
units.literal: In the ninth month of the fifteenth year, the emperor said empire-wide property, since comprehensive inspection more than ten years, rich and poor changed, tax levies light and heavy uneven—sent Jinan Prefect Liang Su and twenty-six others to conduct reorganization by route.

units.zh: 二十年四月，上謂宰臣曰：「猛安謀克戶，富貧差發不均，皆自謀克內科之，暗者惟胥吏之言是從，輕重不一。
units.en: In the fourth month of the twentieth year the emperor told councilors: "Meng'an-mouke corvée falls unevenly because each mouke levies internally and the ignorant follow clerks' word—burdens vary wildly.
units.literal: In the fourth month of the twentieth year, the emperor told grand councilors: "Meng'an mouke households—rich and poor corvée assignments uneven—all levied within the mouke; the ignorant follow only clerks' words, light and heavy not uniform.

units.zh: 自窩斡叛後，貧富反復，今當籍其夾戶，推其家貲，儻有軍役庶可均也。」
units.en: Since Wowohan's rebellion fortunes have reversed; we should register dependent households and assess family wealth so military duties may be fairly shared."
units.literal: Since Wowohan's rebellion, rich and poor reversed; now we should register their dependent households, assess family wealth—if there is military service perhaps it can be even."

units.zh: 詔集百官議，右丞相克甯、平章政事安禮，樞密副使宗尹言：「女直人除猛安謀克僕從差使，余無差役。
units.en: Officials were summoned to debate; Right Grand Councilor Kening, Grand Councilor Anli, and Privy Council Vice Commissioner Zongyin said: "Apart from meng'an-mouke attendant duties, Jurchen bear no other corvée.
units.literal: An edict gathered the hundred officials to discuss; Right Grand Councilor Kening, Grand Councilor Anli, Privy Council Vice Commissioner Zongyin said: "Jurchen apart from meng'an mouke attendant assignments have no other corvée.

units.zh: 今不推奴婢孳畜、地土數目，止驗產業科差為便。」
units.en: Assessing only property for corvée, not counting bond servants, livestock, or land, would be simpler."
units.literal: Now not assessing slaves, livestock, land numbers—only verifying property for corvée assignment is convenient."

units.zh: 左丞相守道等言：「止驗財產，多寡分為四等，置籍以科差，庶得均也。」
units.en: Left Grand Councilor Shoudao and others said: "Verify property alone, divide into four grades, register for corvée—that may achieve fairness."
units.literal: Left Grand Councilor Shoudao and others said: "Only verify property, divide abundance into four grades, set registers for corvée—perhaps it can be even."

units.zh: 左丞通、右丞道、都點檢襄言：「括其奴婢之數，則貧富自見，緩急有事科差，與一例科差者不同。
units.en: Left Vice Councilor Tong, Right Vice Councilor Dao, and Chief Inspector Xiang said: "Count bond servants and wealth becomes visible; urgent and routine corvée differ from lump assessment.
units.literal: Left Vice Councilor Tong, Right Vice Councilor Dao, Chief Inspector Xiang said: "Counting their slaves—then rich and poor show themselves; urgent and routine corvée differ from uniform lump assessment.

units.zh: 請俟農隙，拘括地土牛具之數，各以所見上聞。」
units.en: They asked to wait for the farming slack season, investigate land and ox teams, and report findings."
units.literal: Request waiting for farming slack, investigating land and ox-team numbers, each reporting what they see."

units.zh: 上曰：「一謀克戶之貧富，謀克豈不知。
units.en: The emperor said: "Does not each mouke know its households' wealth?
units.literal: The emperor said: "One mouke household's rich and poor—the mouke surely knows.

units.zh: 一猛安所領八謀克，一例科差。
units.en: Yet one meng'an levies eight mouke uniformly.
units.literal: One meng'an commands eight mouke—uniform lump corvée.

units.zh: 設如一謀無內，有奴婢二三百口者，有奴婢一二人者，科差與同，豈得平均。
units.en: If one household has two or three hundred bond servants and another one or two, yet corvée is the same—how is that fair?
units.literal: Suppose in one mouke within, some have two or three hundred slaves, some one or two slaves—corvée the same; how can it be even?

units.zh: 正隆興兵時，朕之奴婢萬數，孳畜數千，而不差一人一馬，豈可謂平。
units.en: When Zhenglong raised armies I had tens of thousands of bond servants and thousands of livestock yet levied not one man or horse—can that be called fair?
units.literal: When Zhenglong raised armies, Our slaves numbered in the tens of thousands, livestock in the thousands, yet not one person or horse was levied—can this be called even?

units.zh: 朕於庶事未嘗專行，與卿謀之。
units.en: I never decide ordinary affairs alone but deliberate with you.
units.literal: We in ordinary affairs have never acted alone, but deliberated with you.

units.zh: 往年散置契丹戶，安禮極言恐擾動，朕決行之，果得安業。
units.en: When I dispersed Khitan households, Anli warned of unrest; I carried it through and they settled peacefully.
units.literal: In former years dispersing Khitan households, Anli strongly said he feared disturbance; We resolutely carried it out and indeed secured settled livelihoods.

units.zh: 安禮雖盡忠，未審長策。
units.en: Anli is loyal but lacks long-term vision.
units.literal: Anli though utterly loyal did not discern long-term policy.

units.zh: 其從左丞通等所見，拘括推排之。」
units.en: Follow Left Vice Councilor Tong's view—investigate and reassess."
units.literal: Follow Left Vice Councilor Tong and others' view—investigate and conduct reorganization by assessment."

units.zh: 十二月，上謂宰臣曰：「猛安謀克多新強舊弱，差役不均，其令推排，當自中都路始。」
units.en: In the twelfth month the emperor said: "Meng'an-mouke units mix new wealth with old poverty and corvée is uneven—begin reassessment on the Central Capital route."
units.literal: In the twelfth month, the emperor told grand councilors: "Meng'an mouke mostly new strong and old weak, corvée uneven—order reorganization by assessment, starting from the Central Capital route."

units.zh: 至二十二年八月，始詔令集耆老，推貧富，驗土地牛具奴婢之數，分為上中下三等。
units.en: By the eighth month of the twenty-second year elders were gathered to assess wealth, verify land, ox teams, and bond servants, and divide households into upper, middle, and lower grades.
units.literal: By the eighth month of the twenty-second year, they first decreed gathering elders, assessing rich and poor, verifying land, ox teams, and slave numbers, dividing into upper, middle, and lower three grades.

units.zh: 以同知大興府事完顏烏裏也先推中都路，續遣戶部主事按帶等十四人與外官同分路推排。
units.en: Associate Administrator of Daxing Prefecture Wanyan Wuliye led the Central Capital route; Revenue Bureau Administrator Andai and fourteen others joined outer officials on separate routes.
units.literal: With Associate Administrator of Daxing Prefecture Wanyan Wuliye first assessing the Central Capital route, then sending Revenue Bureau Administrator Andai and fourteen others with outer officials to conduct reorganization by route.

units.zh: 九月，詔：「毋令富者匿隱畜產，貧戶或有不敢養馬者。
units.en: In the ninth month the court decreed: "The rich must not conceal livestock, nor should the poor fear keeping horses.
units.literal: In the ninth month, an edict: "Do not let the rich conceal livestock; poor households perhaps dare not keep horses.

units.zh: 昔海陵時，拘括馬畜，絕無等級，富者倖免，貧者盡拘入官，大為不均。
units.en: Under Hailing, horse requisition ignored rank—the rich escaped and the poor lost all stock to the state, a gross injustice.
units.literal: Formerly in Hailing's time, requisitioning horses and livestock had no grades; the rich luckily escaped, the poor all seized into government—greatly uneven.

units.zh: 今並核實貧富造籍，有急即按籍取之，庶幾無不均之弊。」
units.en: Now verify wealth, register livestock, and requisition by register in emergencies—thus avoiding uneven abuse."
units.literal: Now verify rich and poor and make registers; when urgent take from registers—perhaps no uneven abuse."

units.zh: 張汝弼、梁肅奏：「天下民戶通檢既定，設有產物移易，自應隨業輸納。
units.en: Zhang Rubi and Liang Su reported: "Once comprehensive inspection is set, property transfers should pay tax according to the new holder's status.
units.literal: Zhang Rubi and Liang Su reported: "Empire-wide household comprehensive inspection being fixed, if property changes hands, naturally should pay according to occupation.

units.zh: 至於浮財，須有增耗，貧者自貧，富者自富，似不必屢推排也。」
units.en: Floating wealth rises and falls—the poor stay poor, the rich remain rich—so repeated reassessment seems unnecessary."
units.literal: As for floating wealth, there must be increase and decrease; the poor remain poor, the rich remain rich—seemingly no need for repeated reorganization."

units.zh: 上曰：「宰執家多有新富者，故皆不願也。」
units.en: The emperor said: "Councilors' families have grown newly rich—that is why you resist."
units.literal: The emperor said: "Grand councilors' families mostly have newly rich—therefore all are unwilling."

units.zh: 肅對曰：「如臣者，能推排中都物力。
units.en: Su replied: "As for me, I can reassess Central Capital property.
units.literal: Su replied: "As for one like your servant, I can conduct reorganization of Central Capital property.

units.zh: 臣以嘗為南使，先自添物力錢至六十餘貫，視其他奉使無如臣多者。
units.en: I once served as envoy to the Song south and had my property assessment raised by more than sixty strings—more than any other envoy on record.
units.literal: Your servant, having once served as envoy to the south, first added property assessment money to more than sixty strings—viewing other envoys, none had as much as your servant.

units.zh: 但小民無知，法出奸生，數動搖則易駭。
units.en: Yet common people are ignorant; new laws breed evasion, and frequent upheaval easily panics them.
units.literal: But small folk are ignorant; when laws issue, treachery arises; frequent disturbance then easily terrifies.

units.zh: 如唐、宋及遼時，或三二十年不測通比則有之。
units.en: Under Tang, Song, and Liao, comprehensive censuses sometimes came only every twenty or thirty years.
units.literal: As in Tang, Song, and Liao times, sometimes twenty or thirty years might pass without a comprehensive comparison—such cases existed.

units.zh: 頻歲推排，似為難爾。」
units.en: Annual reassessment seems hard to sustain."
units.literal: Reorganization by assessment year after year seems difficult."

units.zh: 二十六年，複以李晏等分路推排。
units.en: In the twenty-sixth year Li Yan and others were again sent on separate routes to reassess property.
units.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, again with Li Yan and others they conducted reorganization by route.

units.zh: 二十七年，奏晏等所定物力之數。
units.en: In the twenty-seventh year they reported the property assessments Yan's team had fixed.
units.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, they reported the property assessment numbers Yan and others had fixed.

units.zh: 上曰：「朕以元推天下物力錢三百五萬餘貫，除三百萬貫外，令減五萬餘貫。
units.en: The emperor said: "The original empire-wide property assessment was over 3.5 million strings; I ordered all but three million reduced by more than fifty thousand.
units.literal: The emperor said: "We originally assessed empire-wide property money at more than 3.5 million strings; apart from three million strings, We ordered a reduction of more than fifty thousand strings.

units.zh: 今減不及數，複續收二萬餘貫，即是實二萬貫爾，而曰續收，何也？」
units.en: The reduction fell short, yet you report another twenty thousand collected as 'continued collection'—that is simply twenty thousand new—why call it otherwise?"
units.literal: Now the reduction did not reach the amount, yet again continued collection of more than twenty thousand strings—this is really twenty thousand strings, yet you call it continued collection—why?"

units.zh: 對曰：「此謂舊脫漏而今首出者，及民地舊無力耕種，而今耕種者也。」
units.en: They replied: "These are cases formerly omitted now first reported, and land the people could not farm before but cultivate now."
units.literal: They replied: "This means those formerly omitted and now first appearing, and commoners' land formerly without strength to cultivate but now cultivated."

units.zh: 上曰：「通檢舊數，止于視其營運息耗，與房地多寡，而加減之。
units.en: The emperor said: "The old comprehensive inspection adjusted only business gains and losses and the amount of houses and land.
units.literal: The emperor said: "Comprehensive inspection's old numbers only looked at their business profit and loss, and houses and land more or less, and increased or decreased accordingly.

units.zh: 彼人賣地，此人買之，皆舊數也。
units.en: When one sells land and another buys, the total should remain the old figure.
units.literal: That person sells land, this person buys it—all old numbers.

units.zh: 至如營運。
units.en: As for business operations,
units.literal: As for business operations.

units.zh: 此強則彼弱，強者增之，弱者減之而已。
units.en: where one grows strong another weakens—raise the strong, lower the weak, and no more.
units.literal: Where this is strong that is weak—the strong are increased, the weak decreased, that is all.
